points.text: States that atoms at the hot end vibrate with larger amplitude
Explains that they collide with their neighbours, passing kinetic energy along atom to atom until the far end warms

items.prompt: One end of a metal rod is held in a flame. A minute later the far end feels warm. Explain, at the particle level, how the energy got there.

points.text: Selects p = nRT / V with n = 0.50 mol, R = 8.31, T = 300 K and V = 0.012 m^3
Computes p = (0.50 x 8.31 x 300) / 0.012 = 1.04 x 10^5 Pa to 3 significant figures

items.prompt: An ideal gas of 0.50 mol is held in a container of volume 0.012 m^3 at 300 K. Calculate its pressure. (R = 8.31 J mol^-1 K^-1)

points.text: Applies Faraday's law: emf = -N x 0.020 / 0.50 = 8.0 V, the minus sign showing the induced emf opposes the change (Lenz's law)

items.prompt: The flux through a 200-turn coil falls from 0.030 Wb to 0.010 Wb in 0.50 s. Calculate the induced emf, showing your working with Faraday's law.

points.text: States that the emf follows the rate of change of flux, not the flux itself

Explains that as the coil turns edge-on the flux passes through zero but is changing fastest there, so the emf peaks, and half a turn later the flux changes the other way so the emf reverses and alternates

items.prompt: In the generator scene the coil spins steadily in a magnetic field. Explain why the induced emf is greatest when the flux through the coil is passing through zero, and why the emf alternates.

levels.descriptor: Methods are chosen and applied exactly, temperature averages and flux changes are stated explicitly, and conclusions are justified without claiming every molecule moves faster in a hotter gas.
levels.label: Secure

levels.descriptor: Method is correct in outline but an average-versus-total, kelvin or flux-change step is skipped.
levels.label: Developing

levels.descriptor: Methods are misapplied - for example claiming every molecule moves faster in a hotter gas - and the working does not support the answer.
levels.label: Beginning
